critical_operation.code_excerpt:
elif (
                self.evalex
                and cmd is not None
                and frame is not None
                and self.secret == secret
                and self.check_pin_trust(environ)
            ):
                response = self.execute_command(request, cmd, frame)  # type: ignore
critical_operation.description: In 3.0.2, DebuggedApplication.__call__ (lines 500-534) dispatches any request carrying `__debugger__=yes` using only query parameters (cmd, f, frm, s) plus self.secret and the pin cookie; it never validates the request Host or Origin against trusted hosts. The evalex branch (520-527) therefore routes an attacker-routed request into execute_command (367-380), which reaches `frame.eval(command)` at line 380 and then `exec()` in console.py. `pin_auth`, `log_pin_request` and `display_console` (`/console`) are likewise unguarded. The fix in 3.0.3 adds `trusted_hosts` (default `.localhost`, `127.0.0.1`) and returns `SecurityError` from those handlers unless `check_host_trust` passes, and also gates the rendered evalex console. The root cause is the absence of these checks, not a defect in the pre-existing `host_is_trusted` helper.

entry_point.description: DebuggedApplication.__call__ dispatches every `?__debugger__=yes` request. For cmd values it requires only that the `s` argument equals self.secret and that check_pin_trust(environ) returns truthy; there is no Host or Origin constraint before calling execute_command. The `/console` path is likewise served by display_console without a host check.
